title: Non-negative remainder
description: Return the remainder r of a divided by b that is never negative: r is the one integer with 0 <= r < |b| for which a - r is a multiple of b. For example -7 and 3 give 2, 7 and 3 give 1, and -7 and -3 give 2 (the sign of b does not matter). b is never 0 and may be negative.
notes: Experiment int_division: hidden tests use negative operands; the description states Euclidean-style non-negative remainder in words. The ref.zehn is written with int.div_floor / int.div_trunc / int.rem_euclid so it is valid under int_ops=operators and int_ops=explicit.
